Chunked full-catalog ranking is exhaustive, but floating-point results need not match unchunked scoring bitwise. PyTorch documents differences between whole-tensor and sliced computations; changing GEMM shapes can change arithmetic order. Consequently, scoring the target separately with an elementwise reduction or narrower matmul can shift its score relative to catalog scores, flip near ties, or even count itself as outranking itself. Recommended approach: obtain the target score from its catalog chunk, then stream comparisons in a second pass using identical shapes and precision; explicitly exclude the target. This is an implementation inference from [PyTorch numerical-accuracy guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).

Disable autocast around scoring, cast both operands to float32, and explicitly select IEEE FP32 matmul using the installed version’s precision controls. Float32 outputs alone do not exclude TF32 internal arithmetic; casting already-rounded embeddings cannot recover lost precision. FP16/BF16 reductions can also overflow. [Precision controls](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/cuda.html). Reject unexpected NaN/Inf before eligibility masking: NaN comparisons can silently undercount outrankers. Define a total order, such as descending score then ascending item ID: rank = 1 + count(score > target_score or (score == target_score and item_id < target_id)), restricted to eligible competitors. Do not introduce epsilon ties. `topk` does not guarantee stable tied indices; [stable sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.sort.html) preserves an explicitly established item-ID order.

Recommended bounded-fixture checks: compare streaming scores, exact ranks and top-k against unchunked float32 scoring across chunk sizes, especially irregular tails; include duplicate embeddings, near ties, exclusions, target boundaries and injected nonfinite values. Score tolerances alone cannot establish rank agreement. Deterministic algorithms improve repeatability but do not guarantee chunk-size or cross-platform equivalence; pin hardware/software and record precision settings. [Reproducibility guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/notes/randomness.html).
